question: Does applying the same input-height fractional hypothesis to surrounding surface visibility and material crossing reduce remaining strong-attenuation errors?
feature_change: Append 20 surrounding-surface and 16 material-crossing descriptors at TX height 3-frac(H_TX).
selection_data: unchanged internal FIT/DEV, same uniform pixels and official masks for loss only
training: Same C10 hyperparameters and seed, max 1200 trees and patience100
promotion_gate: At least 3 percent relative RMSE reduction in EACH band on the unchanged sampled DEV. A failed gate stops this branch; no full refit or official score.
reason: Complete C10 DEV shows about half residual SSE within label and prediction both >=10 dB excess loss. C10 corrects direct profiles but surrounding-surface descriptors retain TX=2/3 endpoints.
code_provenance: Independent code already developed inside CC; no outside-AI artifacts
